advances: An independent rational convex support can destroy the target-scale cutoff bound even for an exact positive definite Gaussian whose unrestricted nearest lattice point is retained. The construction has Hessian identically twice its Gaussian matrix, maximum oriented reflection mass and canonical cutoff score both exactly one, and normalized total mass tending to infinity. Its exact convex-body realizations nevertheless have actual depth at least one half of the weak-Oertel scale. This settles the registered boundary question negatively without refuting the locked target or asserting a limitation for a different scalar or capacity certificate.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The only combinatorial input is the exact general height-profile construction and its all-center bounds from 604889294a17d7df. The weighted integer-centerpoint assertion is used from bb2b5f9519ae23e8. The comparisons with complete Gaussian sublevels and variable Hessian ratios use d7c8f1d06792b00b and 094b111a5dc23b9a, respectively. The Gaussian perturbation, every-center and every-cutoff comparison, support distinction, exact convex-body realization, and actual depth calculation are proved above without a computer certificate.
proof:
Fix an integer \(k\ge8\). Apply the arbitrary rapidly decreasing profile construction of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df to the exact profile \(\rho_t=e^{-t^2}\), for integer \(0\le t\le k\). Its hypotheses hold because \(\rho_0=1\), every weight is positive, and

\[
\frac{\rho_{t+1}}{\rho_t}=e^{-(2t+1)}\le e^{-1}<\frac12
\qquad(0\le t<k).
\tag{4}
\]

Here \(e>2\), for example from the positive series for the exponential at one. Rebuild every entrance count and dimension from this profile. Explicitly, set \(b_\ell=0\) for \(1\le\ell<8\), \(b_\ell=\lfloor e^{\ell^2}/(8\ell)\rfloor\) for \(8\le\ell\le k\), \(Q_0=0\), \(Q_\ell=\sum_{r=1}^{\ell}b_r\), and \(Q=Q_k\). Put \(a_0=0\) and \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\). Set \(m=2(Q+1)^4\), \(n=\sum_{r=1}^Qm^r\), and \(N=n+1\). These are precisely the parameters in 604889294a17d7df after (4); in particular that construction gives \(Q\ge4\), so \(n\ge1\).

Use the exact tree coordinate set \(\mathcal T_{m,Q}\), tree lattice set \(A_{m,Q}\), polytope \(P_{m,Q}\), and level function from 604889294a17d7df, with these rebuilt parameters. No change is made to its Boolean-chain successors or its lattice support. Its height construction is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(x)&=\max\left\{0,\max_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}}
a_{|u|}(x_u-1)\right\},\\
\widehat P&=\{(x,t):x\in P_{m,Q},\ \phi(x)\le t\le k\},\\
D=\widehat P\cap\mathbb Z^N
&=\{(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\ t\in\mathbb Z,
\ a_{\operatorname{level}(z)}\le t\le k\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

The last identity is the complete lattice support assertion of that accepted fact; no lattice points are discarded. The same fact gives \([0,1]^n\subseteq P_{m,Q}\subseteq[0,2]^n\), so \(\phi=0\) on \([0,1]^n\) and the two box inclusions in the statement follow. The polytope \(\widehat P\) is compact, convex, rational, and full-dimensional. In particular, the use of irrational profile values in the entrance counts does not affect rationality: the counts \(b_\ell\), depths, and entrance heights are integers, the tree polytope is the convex hull of integer points, and all additional inequalities in (5) have integer coefficients.

Denote the profile table in 604889294a17d7df by \(w^{(0)}\) here, and its total mass and reflection sums by \(W_0\) and \(S^{(0)}_{\mathbf J}\). Thus \(w^{(0)}_{(z,t)}=e^{-t^2}\) on \(D\), and it is zero elsewhere. This is an explicit alias for that predecessor's \(w,W,S_{\mathbf J}\), leaving the unadorned symbols for the positive definite Gaussian table to be constructed. Its all-center reflection estimate and mass estimate give

\[
S^{(0)}_{\mathbf J}\le1\quad(\mathbf J\in\mathbb Z^N),
\qquad
\frac{W_0}{2^N}\ge\frac3{64}(H_k-H_7).
\tag{6}
\]

Only this accepted general-profile result is used for the tree combinatorics; neither of its two special profile realizations is substituted for the present profile.

Now use \(\varepsilon,A,V\) from the statement, and define the new table by the exact Gaussian formula. For every \((x,t)\in\widehat P\), the box inclusion gives \(0\le\varepsilon\|x\|_2^2\le1\). Consequently, at every integer index, including indices outside the support where both sides vanish,

\[
e^{-1}w^{(0)}_{\mathbf I}\le w_{\mathbf I}\le w^{(0)}_{\mathbf I},
\qquad
W\ge e^{-1}W_0,
\qquad
S_{\mathbf J}\le S^{(0)}_{\mathbf J}\le1
\quad(\mathbf J\in\mathbb Z^N).
\tag{7}
\]

The reflection comparison follows term by term because taking the minimum is increasing in each endpoint weight. It covers all integer centers and both orientations, not just a selected center. The support remains exactly \(D\). If a center outside \(D\) had two positive reflected endpoints, their midpoint would belong to the convex set \(\widehat P\) and be an integer point, contradicting (5); thus such centers also have zero reflection sum.

The matrix \(A\) is symmetric, rational, and positive definite because \(\varepsilon>0\). Hence \(V\ge0\) on all of \(\mathbb R^N\), with equality precisely at zero. The point zero belongs to \([0,1]^n\times[0,k]\), so \(w_0=1\), and zero is the unique minimizer even before the lattice restriction or the support restriction. The global Hessian is exactly \(2A\).

For \(\mathbf J\in D\) and \(v=(v',u)\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\), both endpoints retain their exact Gaussian weights, and direct quadratic expansion gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_{\mathbf J}(v)
&=V(\mathbf J+v)+V(\mathbf J-v)-2V(\mathbf J)\\
&=2v^{\mathsf T}Av
=2\varepsilon\|v'\|_2^2+2u^2
=2V(v)\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]

It vanishes only at \(v=0\). The finite support makes every displacement domain finite, and zero is present at each supported center. For any cutoff \(L\ge0\), replacing \(L\) by the largest actual curvature at most \(L\) leaves the numerator unchanged and decreases the denominator. The maxima defining \(K_{\mathbf J}\) and \(K\) therefore exist. At every center and cutoff, (7) gives \(B_{\mathbf J}^{\Delta}(L)/(1+L)\le S_{\mathbf J}\le1\). At the supported center zero with cutoff zero, (8) gives \(B_0^{\Delta}(0)=w_0=1\). Thus \(K(w)=1\). Also \(S_0\ge w_0=1\), so (7) gives \(\max_{\mathbf J}S_{\mathbf J}=1\). Combining (6) and (7) proves all inequalities in (1). Since \(H_k-H_7\ge\int_8^{k+1}dx/x\to\infty\), they give the asserted limit. For any proposed \(c>0\), taking \(k\) with the upper bound on the ratio in (1) less than \(c\) disproves \(K(w)\ge c\,2^{-N}W\).

We verify the exact distinction from a complete energy cutoff. Let \(e_1\) be one tree-coordinate unit vector in \(\mathbb R^n\). The point \((e_1,0)\) belongs to \([0,1]^n\times[0,k]\subseteq\widehat P\), whereas \((-e_1,0)\) does not belong to \([0,2]^n\times[0,k]\) and hence does not belong to \(\widehat P\). Their energies are both \(\varepsilon\). Any complete lattice energy sublevel containing the first must contain the second. This proves that (5) cannot equal a complete energy sublevel for any \(R\), although the unrestricted minimizer zero is retained.

In the Gaussian part of accepted fact d7c8f1d06792b00b, substitute \(N\) for its integer dimension, use the present matrix \(A\), and identify the quadratic form called \(Q(v)\) there with the present energy \(V(v)\). Its theorem gives an absolute lower bound for complete energy sublevels with this matrix and \(\kappa=1\); (5) fails precisely the completeness hypothesis just checked. The analytic regularization obstruction of accepted fact 094b111a5dc23b9a instead uses nonquadratic potentials and complete energy sublevels, and its admissible Hessian comparison ratios must diverge. In the present construction \(\nabla^2V\equiv2A\) on the whole real space, so no variable relative Hessian ratio is involved. The independent convex boundary is an additional obstruction. The variation in the entries of \(A\) does not alter this conclusion: the reference-metric ratio used by d7c8f1d06792b00b is exactly one for every member.

We next prove that (2) is an exact actual-body realization. On \(\widehat P\), the energy satisfies \(0\le V\le k^2+1\). Fix an integer \(d\ge2(k^2+1)\) and put \(f(\xi)=e^{-V(\xi)/d}\) for real \(\xi\in\mathbb R^N\). At any such \(\xi\), put \(g=\nabla V(\xi)=2A\xi\). For every real direction \(u\), Cauchy-Schwarz in the positive definite form \(A\) gives

\[
(u^{\mathsf T}g)^2
=4(u^{\mathsf T}A\xi)^2
\le4V(\xi)u^{\mathsf T}Au
=2V(\xi)u^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2V(\xi)u.
\tag{9}
\]

Thus \(gg^{\mathsf T}\preceq2V(\xi)\nabla^2V(\xi)\), and on \(\widehat P\),

\[
\nabla^2 f(\xi)
=\frac{f(\xi)}{d^2}\bigl(gg^{\mathsf T}-d\nabla^2V(\xi)\bigr)
\preceq\frac{f(\xi)}{d^2}(2V(\xi)-d)\nabla^2V(\xi)
\preceq0.
\tag{10}
\]

The ordinary second-derivative criterion on every segment in the convex polytope \(\widehat P\) proves that \(f\) is concave there, including the boundary. If \((\xi,y)\) and \((\xi',y')\) belong to (2), then for \(0\le\lambda\le1\), their interpolated base lies in \(\widehat P\), and each continuous coordinate satisfies

\[
|(1-\lambda)y_i+\lambda y_i'|
\le\frac{(1-\lambda)f(\xi)+\lambda f(\xi')}{2}
\le\frac{f((1-\lambda)\xi+\lambda\xi')}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]

This proves convexity of (2). The base is compact, the inequalities are closed and continuous, and \(f\le1\) there, so the body is closed and bounded. Also \(f\ge e^{-(k^2+1)/d}>0\) everywhere on the base. The base contains the full-dimensional box \([0,1]^n\times[0,k]\), so (2) contains the product of its interior with an open continuous box of positive side length. It is therefore full-dimensional.

For every real \(\xi\in\widehat P\), the fiber in (2) is the centered cube of side length \(f(\xi)\) and volume \(f(\xi)^d=e^{-V(\xi)}\). Outside \(\widehat P\), the fiber is empty. Together with the complete lattice census (5), this proves every claimed integer volume exactly. At boundary points the side length is still positive; no boundary fibers were removed or replaced by a zero-volume convention. Compactness gives finitely many integer fibers, and hence \(\mathcal H_d(\mathcal S)=W>0\).

Finally define the finite positive base measure \(\nu=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I}\delta_{\mathbf I}\). The weighted integer-centerpoint argument proved in accepted fact bb2b5f9519ae23e8, with its integer dimension \(n\) replaced by \(N\), supplies a point \(\mathbf J_0\in\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^N\) such that every proper closed base halfspace containing \(\mathbf J_0\) has \(\nu\)-mass at least \(2^{-N}W\). This is the predecessor's weighted integer assertion, with unchanged weight normalization. Since \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\subseteq\widehat P\) and \(D=\widehat P\cap\mathbb Z^N\), the point \(\mathbf J_0\) belongs to \(D\). Fix \(p=(\mathbf J_0,0)\in\mathcal S\) before choosing an ambient halfspace.

Let \(H\) be any proper closed ambient halfspace containing \(p\). It has a representation

\[
H=\{(\xi,y):a^{\mathsf T}(\xi-\mathbf J_0)+b^{\mathsf T}y\ge\tau\},
\qquad \tau\le0,\quad(a,b)\ne(0,0).
\]

Replacing \(\tau\) by zero gives a through-point halfspace \(H_0\subseteq H\). Put \(G=\{\xi:a^{\mathsf T}(\xi-\mathbf J_0)\ge0\}\). If \(a\ne0\), the chosen base center gives \(\nu(G)\ge2^{-N}W\). If \(a=0\), then \(G=\mathbb R^N\) and \(\nu(G)=W\), so the same lower bound holds.

For every \(\mathbf I\in D\cap G\), the section of \(H_0\) in its fiber contains the part with \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\). If \(b\ne0\), the reflection \(y\mapsto-y\) preserves the centered cube and its volume and exchanges its intersections with \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\). These two closed parts cover the cube, so each has at least half its volume. If \(b=0\), the whole fiber is retained, which also gives the half-volume bound. Summing these nonnegative contributions yields

\[
\mathcal H_d(\mathcal S\cap H)
\ge\mathcal H_d(\mathcal S\cap H_0)
\ge\frac12\sum_{\mathbf I\in D\cap G}w_{\mathbf I}
=\frac12\nu(G)
\ge\frac{W}{2^{N+1}}.
\tag{12}
\]

The whole ambient space, if included among halfspaces, satisfies the same bound. Every defining halfspace inequality was weak; in particular vertical halfspaces retain the full fibers on their boundaries, and no positive boundary mixed mass was discarded. The point \(p\) was fixed independently of \(H\). Taking the infimum proves (3). Since \(1/e<1/2\), each of these actual bodies satisfies the locked depth bound for every allowed \(c_0\), even though its canonical scalar ratio tends to zero.
statement:
The integer dimension in the registered subgoal and in the locked problem is denoted by \(N\) here. The symbol \(n\) is the number of tree coordinates in accepted fact 604889294a17d7df, and \(N=n+1\). The symbol \(Q\) denotes that predecessor's tree depth throughout. Gaussian energy is denoted by \(V\), never by \(Q\). The continuous dimension retains the locked problem's symbol \(d\).

For a compact convex polytope \(\widehat P\subset\mathbb R^N\) containing zero and a symmetric positive definite matrix \(A\), set \(V(\xi)=\xi^{\mathsf T}A\xi\), \(D=\widehat P\cap\mathbb Z^N\), \(w_{\mathbf I}=e^{-V(\mathbf I)}\mathbf1_D(\mathbf I)\), and \(W=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\mathbb Z^N}w_{\mathbf I}\). Retain the canonical definitions of accepted facts 604889294a17d7df and d7c8f1d06792b00b:

\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathbf J}&=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^N}\min\{w_{\mathbf J+v},w_{\mathbf J-v}\}
&& (\mathbf J\in\mathbb Z^N),\\
\alpha(v)&=\min\{w_{\mathbf J+v},w_{\mathbf J-v}\},
&\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}&=\{v\in\mathbb Z^N:\alpha(v)>0\},\\
\Delta_{\mathbf J}(v)&=\log\frac{w_{\mathbf J}^2}{w_{\mathbf J+v}w_{\mathbf J-v}}
&& (\mathbf J\in D,\ v\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}),\\
B_{\mathbf J}^{\Delta}(L)&=
\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\\\Delta_{\mathbf J}(v)\le L}}\alpha(v),
&K_{\mathbf J}(w)&=\max_{L\ge0}\frac{B_{\mathbf J}^{\Delta}(L)}{1+L},\\
K(w)&=\max_{\mathbf J\in D}K_{\mathbf J}(w).
\end{aligned}
\]

In the definitions of \(\alpha\) and \(\mathcal U_{\mathbf J}\), the center \(\mathbf J\in D\) is fixed and its dependence is suppressed. Displacement sums are oriented, include both signs of a nonzero displacement, and include zero exactly once. All logarithms are natural. These definitions use the integer dimension \(N\) in place of the dimension \(n\) in d7c8f1d06792b00b.

For every integer \(k\ge8\), the construction in the proof gives finite positive integers \(n,N=n+1\), a compact full-dimensional rational polytope \(\widehat P\), and the rational positive definite matrix

\[
\varepsilon=\frac1{4n},\qquad
A=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon I_n,1),\qquad
V(x,t)=\varepsilon\|x\|_2^2+t^2,
\]

such that \([0,1]^n\times[0,k]\subseteq\widehat P\subseteq[0,2]^n\times[0,k]\). Thus zero belongs to the support and is the unique unrestricted lattice minimizer of \(V\). With all parameters reconstructed for each \(k\), the resulting exact Gaussian table satisfies

\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\mathbf J\in\mathbb Z^N}S_{\mathbf J}=K(w)&=1,\\
\frac W{2^N}&\ge\frac{3}{64e}(H_k-H_7),\\
0<\frac{2^N K(w)}W&\le\frac{64e}{3(H_k-H_7)}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad H_k=\sum_{\ell=1}^k\frac1\ell.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

For every supported center \(\mathbf J\) and every positive reflected pair, \(\Delta_{\mathbf J}(v)=2V(v)\). Globally, \(\nabla^2V\equiv2A\), so its Hessian comparison ratio relative to \(A\) is exactly \(\kappa=1\). Nevertheless, no energy level \(R\) has \(D=\{\mathbf I\in\mathbb Z^N:V(\mathbf I)\le R\}\).

For every positive integer \(d\ge2(k^2+1)\), define

\[
C^{\mathrm G}_{k,d}
=\left\{(x,t,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d:
(x,t)\in\widehat P,\quad
|y_i|\le\frac12e^{-V(x,t)/d}\ (1\le i\le d)\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]

This is a compact full-dimensional convex body. Its exact actual fiber volumes, including the positive fibers above every boundary lattice point and the zero volumes outside \(D\), are \(\operatorname{vol}_d((C^{\mathrm G}_{k,d})_{\mathbf I})=w_{\mathbf I}\). The superscript distinguishes this Gaussian realization from the different bodies \(C_{k,d}\) in 604889294a17d7df.

Let \(\mathcal S=C^{\mathrm G}_{k,d}\cap(\mathbb Z^N\times\mathbb R^d)\), which is the set called \(S\) in the locked problem for this body. There is one \(\mathbf J_0\in D\), chosen before the ambient halfspace, such that

\[
h_{\mathcal S}((\mathbf J_0,0))
\ge\frac{W}{2^{N+1}}.
\tag{3}
\]

The depth in (3) uses every closed ambient halfspace containing the selected point, including vertical halfspaces and halfspaces whose boundaries carry positive mixed mass. In particular, (1) disproves every absolute positive lower coefficient for \(K(w)/(2^{-N}W)\) under arbitrary rational convex truncation with the nearest lattice point retained, while these actual bodies satisfy the locked depth inequality for every \(c_0\in(0,1/e)\).
